To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the actor-network approach provides a powerful conceptual framework for the analysis of organizational change, (2) it is particularly suited to the analysis of change in the context of the development of information systems, and (3) it can be used to analyze change in the context not only of information systems development, but also in the context of organizational development in general.

(1) the social world is composed of heterogeneous networks of human and non-human actors, (2) these networks are not simply the result of human agency, but rather are generated by a complex set of relations between human and non-human agents, and (3) the study of these networks is a key to understanding the social world and to developing a new approach to social theory.

the way in which the social and the material are mutually constituted in the actor networks that are the basic unit of analysis in this approach.
the way in which the social is generated and reproduced through the heterogeneous networks which link together the human and the nonhuman.
the ways in which social and technical networks are formed, how they are stabilized, and how they are reconfigured.
